curriculum.title: Job: Suffering Is Not a Simple Formula

core.big_idea: Job rejects the claim that every instance of suffering is direct punishment for personal sin.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

claims.statement: The opening of Job explicitly presents Job as upright while also showing that his suffering is not explained to him as punishment for a secret sin.
God’s speeches widen Job’s perspective without giving him a simple causal formula for his suffering.
Taken together, these passages support the lesson’s big idea: Job rejects the claim that every instance of suffering is direct punishment for personal sin.

core.interpretation_skill: Locate on timeline; read immediate context; identify genre; separate observation and application

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that job rejects the claim that every instance of suffering is direct punishment for personal sin and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: Job rejects the claim that every instance of suffering is direct punishment for personal sin.
The lesson belongs in Wisdom and Worship.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before interpretation.

become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
